correctness.rationale: The primitive shortest-vector lattice identity makes the normalized quotient-product exactly the area ratio K/P. In the diamond normalization any point exceeding gauge 1+t forces two disjoint exterior triangles with combined area t, so t <= 2 epsilon. The explicit six-vertex family has epsilon=t/2 and P-gauge 1+t; exact-rational checks confirm polygon instances. Boundary choices and zero-deficit rigidity are covered analytically.

value.rationale: Turns a recent scalar lattice-covering near-equality inequality into a precise global affine-invariant geometric stability theorem with an explicit canonical witness, exact optimal order and universal coefficient, zero-deficit rigidity, and matching genuine symmetric hexagonal examples. It applies to all nonsmooth planar symmetric bodies and connects lattice minimization to Hausdorff-type containment. This goes beyond a routine recomputation of the known scalar inequality.
